sanskrit: manoḥ prajāpate rājann ikṣvākur abhavat sutaḥ tasya putraśataṃ jajñe nṛpateḥ sūryavarcasaḥ
english: O king, of Manu the Prajāpati was born a son named Ikṣvāku; and to that king, radiant as the sun, a hundred sons were born.

sanskrit: daśamas tasya putras tu daśāśvo nāma bhārata māhiṣmatyām abhūd rājā dharmātmā satyavikramaḥ
english: His tenth son, O descendant of Bharata, was named Daśāśva; righteous of soul and true in valour, he became king in Māhiṣmatī.

sanskrit: daśāśvasya sutas tv āsīd rājā paramadhārmikaḥ satye tapasi dāne ca yasya nityaṃ rataṃ manaḥ
english: Daśāśva had a son who was a most righteous king, one whose mind was ever devoted to truth, to austerity, and to giving.

sanskrit: madirāśva iti khyātaḥ pṛthivyāṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ dhanurvede ca vede ca nirato yo 'bhavat sadā
english: Renowned upon the earth as Madirāśva, lord of the earth, he was ever absorbed in the science of archery and in the Veda.

sanskrit: madirāśvasya putras tu dyutimān nāma pārthivaḥ mahābhāgo mahātejā mahāsattvo mahābalaḥ
english: Madirāśva's son was a king named Dyutimān, greatly fortunate, of great splendour, great courage, and great strength.

sanskrit: putro dyutimatas tv āsīt suvīro nāma pārthivaḥ dharmātmā kośavāṃś cāpi devarāja ivāparaḥ
english: Dyutimān had a son, a king named Suvīra, righteous of soul and rich in treasure, like a second king of the gods.

sanskrit: suvīrasya tu putro 'bhūt sarvasaṃgrāmadurjayaḥ durjayety abhivikhyātaḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ
english: Suvīra's son, unconquerable in every battle, was famed by the name Durjaya and skilled in all the sciences.

sanskrit: durjayasyendravapuṣaḥ putro 'gnisadṛśadyutiḥ duryodhano nāma mahān rājāsīd rājasattama
english: Durjaya, who had the form of Indra, had a son with the splendour of fire, a great king named Duryodhana, O best of kings.

sanskrit: tasyendrasamavīryasya saṃgrāmeṣv anivartinaḥ viṣayaś ca prabhāvaś ca tulyam evābhyavartata
english: For him, equal to Indra in might and never turning back in battle, his dominion and his power advanced together in equal measure.

sanskrit: ratnair dhanaiś ca paśubhiḥ sasyaiś cāpi pṛthagvidhaiḥ nagaraṃ viṣayaś cāsya pratipūrṇaṃ tadābhavat
english: With jewels, with wealth, with cattle, and with grains of every kind, his city and his realm then became full to overflowing.

sanskrit: na tasya viṣaye cābhūt kṛpaṇo nāpi durgataḥ vyādhito vā kṛśo vāpi tasmin nābhūn naraḥ kva cit
english: In his realm there was no wretched man, nor any fallen on hard times; not anywhere in it was there a man sick or wasted away.

sanskrit: sudakṣiṇo madhuravāg anasūyur jitendriyaḥ dharmātmā cānṛśaṃsaś ca vikrānto 'thāvikatthanaḥ
english: Generous with gifts, sweet of speech, free from envy, master of his senses, righteous of soul, gentle, valiant, yet given to no boasting,

sanskrit: yajvā vadānyo medhāvī brahmaṇyaḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ na cāvamantā dātā ca vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ
english: a performer of sacrifices, liberal, wise, devoted to the brahmins, true to his word, despising none and ever giving, and one who had mastered the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences.

sanskrit: taṃ narmadā devanadī puṇyā śītajalā śivā cakame puruṣaśreṣṭhaṃ svena bhāvena bhārata
english: Him, the best of men, the divine river Narmadā—holy, cool-watered, and auspicious—desired of her own accord, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: tasya jajñe tadā nadyāṃ kanyā rājīvalocanā nāmnā sudarśanā rājan rūpeṇa ca sudarśanā
english: To him then upon that river was born a lotus-eyed daughter, named Sudarśanā, O king, and Sudarśanā—fair to behold—indeed in beauty.

sanskrit: tādṛgrūpā na nārīṣu bhūtapūrvā yudhiṣṭhira duryodhanasutā yādṛg abhavad varavarṇinī
english: Never before among women, O Yudhiṣṭhira, had there been one of such beauty as this daughter of Duryodhana proved to be, that lady of fairest hue.

sanskrit: tām agniś cakame sākṣād rājakanyāṃ sudarśanām bhūtvā ca brāhmaṇaḥ sākṣād varayām āsa taṃ nṛpam
english: Her, the princess Sudarśanā, Agni himself desired; and taking the very form of a brahmin, he sought her hand of that king.

sanskrit: daridraś cāsavarṇaś ca mamāyam iti pārthivaḥ na ditsati sutāṃ tasmai tāṃ viprāya sudarśanām
english: "This man is poor and not of my caste"—so thinking, the king was unwilling to give his daughter Sudarśanā to that brahmin.

sanskrit: tato 'sya vitate yajñe naṣṭo 'bhūd dhavyavāhanaḥ tato duryodhano rājā vākyam āhartvijas tadā
english: Thereupon, while his sacrifice was being performed, the bearer of oblations vanished; and then King Duryodhana spoke these words to the priests:

sanskrit: duṣkṛtaṃ mama kiṃ nu syād bhavatāṃ vā dvijarṣabhāḥ yena nāśaṃ jagāmāgniḥ kṛtaṃ kupuruṣeṣv iva
english: "What evil deed can there be of mine, or of yours, O bulls among the twice-born, by which the fire has gone to ruin, as though a service were rendered to base men?"

sanskrit: na hy alpaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ no 'sti yenāgnir nāśam āgataḥ bhavatāṃ vātha vā mahyaṃ tattvenaitad vimṛśyatām
english: "For no small misdeed is this by which the fire has come to ruin—whether yours or mine; let this be pondered in its very truth."

sanskrit: etad rājño vacaḥ śrutvā viprās te bharatarṣabha niyatā vāgyatāś caiva pāvakaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ
english: Hearing this speech of the king, those brahmins, O bull of the Bhāratas, restrained and controlled in speech, took refuge with the Purifier, the fire.

sanskrit: tān darśayām āsa tadā bhagavān havyavāhanaḥ svaṃ rūpaṃ dīptimat kṛtvā śaradarkasamadyutiḥ
english: Then the blessed bearer of oblations showed himself to them, assuming his own blazing form, radiant as the autumn sun.

sanskrit: tato mahātmā tān āha dahano brāhmaṇarṣabhān varayāmy ātmano 'rthāya duryodhanasutām iti
english: Then the great-souled Consumer addressed those bulls among brahmins: "For my own sake I seek the hand of Duryodhana's daughter."

sanskrit: tatas te kālyam utthāya tasmai rājñe nyavedayan brāhmaṇā vismitāḥ sarve yad uktaṃ citrabhānunā
english: Then, rising at daybreak, those brahmins, all of them astonished, made known to the king what had been said by the One of Wondrous Rays.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā tac chrutvā vacanaṃ brahmavādinām avāpya paramaṃ harṣaṃ tatheti prāha buddhimān
english: Then that king, hearing this speech of the expounders of the Veda, attained the highest joy, and the wise one said, "So be it."

sanskrit: prāyācata nṛpaḥ śulkaṃ bhagavantaṃ vibhāvasum nityaṃ sāṃnidhyam iha te citrabhāno bhaved iti tam āha bhagavān agnir evam astv iti pārthivam
english: The king asked of the blessed Vibhāvasu a bride-price: "Let your perpetual presence be here, O One of Wondrous Rays." And the blessed Agni answered the king, "So be it."

sanskrit: tataḥ sāṃnidhyam adhyāpi māhiṣmatyāṃ vibhāvasoḥ dṛṣṭaṃ hi sahadevena diśo vijayatā tadā
english: Thus even now the presence of Vibhāvasu abides in Māhiṣmatī; for it was seen by Sahadeva when he was conquering the quarters in that day.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃ samalaṃkṛtya kanyām ahatavāsasam dadau duryodhano rājā pāvakāya mahātmane
english: Then King Duryodhana, having adorned the maiden in unworn garments, gave her to the great-souled Purifier.

sanskrit: pratijagrāha cāgnis tāṃ rājaputrīṃ sudarśanām vidhinā vedadṛṣṭena vasor dhārām ivādhvare
english: And Agni received that princess Sudarśanā by the rite ordained in the Veda, as he receives the stream of wealth in the sacrifice.

sanskrit: tasyā rūpeṇa śīlena kulena vapuṣā śriyā abhavat prītimān agnir garbhaṃ tasyāṃ samādadhe
english: Pleased with her beauty, her conduct, her lineage, her form, and her grace, Agni was filled with delight and placed an embryo within her.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ samabhavat putro nāmnāgneyaḥ sudarśanaḥ śiśur evādhyagāt sarvaṃ sa ca brahma sanātanam
english: In her was born a son, by name Sudarśana, son of Agni; while still a child he mastered all the eternal sacred lore.

sanskrit: athaughavān nāma nṛpo nṛgasyāsīt pitāmahaḥ tasyāpy oghavatī kanyā putraś caugharatho 'bhavat
english: Now there was a king named Oghavān, grandfather of Nṛga; and to him belonged a daughter, Oghavatī, and a son named Ogharatha.

sanskrit: tām oghavān dadau tasmai svayam oghavatīṃ sutām sudarśanāya viduṣe bhāryārthe devarūpiṇīm
english: That daughter Oghavatī, of divine beauty, Oghavān himself gave in marriage to the learned Sudarśana, to be his wife.

sanskrit: sa gṛhasthāśramaratas tayā saha sudarśanaḥ kurukṣetre 'vasad rājann oghavatyā samanvitaḥ
english: Sudarśana, devoted to the householder's order of life, dwelt with her in Kurukṣetra, O king, together with Oghavatī.

sanskrit: gṛhasthaś cāvajeṣyāmi mṛtyum ity eva sa prabho pratijñām akarod dhīmān dīptatejā viśāṃ pate
english: "As a householder I shall conquer Death"—so, O lord, that wise one of blazing splendour made his vow, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: tām athaughavatīṃ rājan sa pāvakasuto 'bravīt atitheḥ pratikūlaṃ te na kartavyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: Then, O king, the son of the Purifier said to that Oghavatī: "Nothing contrary to a guest's wish must ever be done by you."

sanskrit: yena yena ca tuṣyeta nityam eva tvayātithiḥ apy ātmanaḥ pradānena na te kāryā vicāraṇā
english: "By whatever means a guest may be satisfied, by that you must always satisfy him—even by the giving of your own self; let there be no hesitation in you."

sanskrit: etad vrataṃ mama sadā hṛdi saṃparivartate gṛhasthānāṃ hi suśroṇi nātither vidyate param
english: "This vow forever turns within my heart; for householders, O fair-hipped one, there is nothing higher than the guest."

sanskrit: pramāṇaṃ yadi vāmoru vacas te mama śobhane idaṃ vacanam avyagrā hṛdi tvaṃ dhārayeḥ sadā
english: "If my word is your standard, O fair-thighed and lovely one, then hold this saying ever in your heart with a steady mind."

sanskrit: niṣkrānte mayi kalyāṇi tathā saṃnihite 'naghe nātithis te 'vamantavyaḥ pramāṇaṃ yady ahaṃ tava
english: "Whether I have gone forth, O auspicious one, or am near at hand, O blameless lady, no guest of yours must be slighted—if indeed I am your standard."

sanskrit: tam abravīd oghavatī yatā mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ na me tvadvacanāt kiṃ cid akartavyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: To him Oghavatī, with restrained mind and palms joined at her brow, replied: "There is nothing whatsoever, set by your word, that I will leave undone."

sanskrit: jigīṣamāṇaṃ tu gṛhe tadā mṛtyuḥ sudarśanam pṛṣṭhato 'nvagamad rājan randhrānveṣī tadā sadā
english: But Death, O king, ever seeking a weak point, then followed close behind Sudarśana as he strove to conquer him there within his house.

sanskrit: idhmārthaṃ tu gate tasminn agniputre sudarśane atithir brāhmaṇaḥ śrīmāṃs tām āhaughavatīṃ tadā
english: Now when that son of Agni, Sudarśana, had gone out for firewood, a guest, a glorious brahmin, then said to Oghavatī:

sanskrit: ātithyaṃ dattam icchāmi tvayādya varavarṇini pramāṇaṃ yadi dharmas te gṛhasthāśramasaṃmataḥ
english: "I wish hospitality given me by you this day, O lady of fairest hue, if the dharma approved for the householder's order is your standard."

sanskrit: ity uktā tena vipreṇa rājaputrī yaśasvinī vidhinā pratijagrāha vedoktena viśāṃ pate
english: Thus addressed by that brahmin, the renowned princess received him by the rite ordained in the Veda, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: āsanaṃ caiva pādyaṃ ca tasmai dattvā dvijātaye provācaughavatī vipraṃ kenārthaḥ kiṃ dadāmi te
english: Having given a seat and water for the feet to that twice-born one, Oghavatī said to the brahmin: "What is your need? What shall I give you?"

sanskrit: tām abravīt tato vipro rājaputrīṃ sudarśanām tvayā mamārthaḥ kalyāṇi nirviśaṅke tad ācara
english: Then the brahmin said to her, the princess Sudarśanā: "My need is of you yourself, O auspicious one; do this without any misgiving."

sanskrit: yadi pramāṇaṃ dharmas te gṛhasthāśramasaṃmataḥ pradānenātmano rājñi kartum arhasi me priyam
english: "If the dharma approved for the householder's order is your standard, O queen, then by the giving of your own self you ought to do me this pleasure."

sanskrit: tathā saṃchandyamāno 'nyair īpsitair nṛpakanyayā nānyam ātmapradānāt sa tasyā vavre varaṃ dvijaḥ
english: Though pressed by the princess with other desirable offerings, that brahmin chose from her no boon but the giving of her own self.

sanskrit: sā tu rājasutā smṛtvā bhartur vacanam āditaḥ tatheti lajjamānā sā tam uvāca dvijarṣabham
english: But the princess, recalling from the first her husband's word, said to that bull among the twice-born, abashed, "So be it."

sanskrit: tato rahaḥ sa viprarṣiḥ sā caivopaviveśa ha saṃsmṛtya bhartur vacanaṃ gṛhasthāśramakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Then that brahmin sage and she, remembering the word of her husband, who longed to keep the householder's order, withdrew together into privacy.

sanskrit: athedhmān samupādāya sa pāvakir upāgamat mṛtyunā raudrabhāvena nityaṃ bandhur ivānvitaḥ
english: Then the son of the Purifier, having gathered the firewood, drew near, attended ever by Death of fearsome aspect, as though by a kinsman.

sanskrit: tatas tv āśramam āgamya sa pāvakasutas tadā tām ājuhāvaughavatīṃ kvāsi yāteti cāsakṛt
english: Then, having come to the hermitage, the son of the Purifier called out to Oghavatī again and again, "Where are you? Where have you gone?"

sanskrit: tasmai prativacaḥ sā tu bhartre na pradadau tadā karābhyāṃ tena vipreṇa spṛṣṭā bhartṛvratā satī
english: But she gave no answer then to her husband, that faithful wife, devoted to her lord, having been touched by the two hands of that brahmin.

sanskrit: ucchiṣṭāsmīti manvānā lajjitā bhartur eva ca tūṣṇīṃbhūtābhavat sādhvī na covācātha kiṃ cana
english: Thinking "I am defiled," and ashamed before her husband, the virtuous one kept silent and said nothing at all.

sanskrit: atha tāṃ punar evedaṃ provāca sa sudarśanaḥ kva sā sādhvī kva sā yātā garīyaḥ kim ato mama
english: Then Sudarśana spoke this to her once more: "Where is that virtuous one? Where has she gone? What is dearer to me than she?"

sanskrit: pativratā satyaśīlā nityaṃ caivārjave ratā kathaṃ na pratyudety adya smayamānā yathā purā
english: "Devoted to her lord, truthful in nature, ever delighting in uprightness—why does she not come forth to meet me today, smiling as of old?"

sanskrit: uṭajasthas tu taṃ vipraḥ pratyuvāca sudarśanam atithiṃ viddhi saṃprāptaṃ pāvake brāhmaṇaṃ ca mām
english: But the brahmin, standing within the leaf-hut, answered Sudarśana: "Know that a guest has arrived, O son of the Purifier, and that I am a brahmin."

sanskrit: anayā chandyamāno 'haṃ bhāryayā tava sattama tais tair atithisatkārair ārjave 'syā dṛḍhaṃ manaḥ
english: "I was entreated by this wife of yours, O excellent one, with this and that mark of honour due to a guest; firm is her mind in uprightness."

sanskrit: anena vidhinā seyaṃ mām arcati śubhānanā anurūpaṃ yad atrādya tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: "By this observance does this fair-faced one honour me; what is fitting here today, that you ought now to declare."

sanskrit: kūṭamudgarahastas tu mṛtyus taṃ vai samanvayāt hīnapratijñam atrainaṃ vadhiṣyāmīti cintayan
english: And Death, a heavy mallet in his hand, attended close upon him, thinking, "Should he here fall short of his vow, I shall slay him."

sanskrit: sudarśanas tu manasā karmaṇā cakṣuṣā girā tyakterṣyas tyaktamanyuś ca smayamāno 'bravīd idam
english: But Sudarśana, in mind, in deed, in glance, and in word free of jealousy and free of wrath, smiling, spoke thus:

sanskrit: surataṃ te 'stu viprāgrya prītir hi paramā mama gṛhasthasya hi dharmo 'gryaḥ saṃprāptātithipūjanam
english: "Let your union be a joy, O foremost of brahmins, for my delight is supreme; the householder's highest dharma is the honouring of a guest who has come."

sanskrit: atithiḥ pūjito yasya gṛhasthasya tu gacchati nānyas tasmāt paro dharma iti prāhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: "The householder from whose house an honoured guest departs satisfied—no dharma higher than this, so the wise declare."

sanskrit: prāṇā hi mama dārāś ca yac cānyad vidyate vasu atithibhyo mayā deyam iti me vratam āhitam
english: "My life-breaths, my wife, and whatever other wealth there is—all this is to be given by me to guests: such is the vow I have taken."

sanskrit: niḥsaṃdigdhaṃ mayā vākyam etat te samudāhṛtam tenāhaṃ vipra satyena svayam ātmānam ālabhe
english: "Without any doubt has this word of mine been uttered to you; by that truth, O brahmin, I myself take hold of my own self."

sanskrit: pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyotiś ca pañcamam buddhir ātmā manaḥ kālo diśaś caiva guṇā daśa
english: "Earth, air, ether, the waters, and fire as the fifth; intellect, self, mind, time, and the quarters of space—these are the ten witnesses."

sanskrit: nityam ete hi paśyanti dehināṃ dehasaṃśritāḥ sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ cāpi karma dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: "For these, abiding within the bodies of embodied beings, ever behold the deeds of men, both good and ill, O best of the upholders of dharma."

sanskrit: yathaiṣā nānṛtā vāṇī mayādya samudāhṛtā tena satyena māṃ devāḥ pālayantu dahantu vā
english: "As surely as this speech uttered by me this day is no falsehood, by that truth let the gods either protect me or consume me."

sanskrit: tato nādaḥ samabhavad dikṣu sarvāsu bhārata asakṛt satyam ity eva naitan mithyeti sarvaśaḥ
english: Then a sound arose in all the quarters, O descendant of Bharata, again and again: "It is true! This is no falsehood!"—on every side.

sanskrit: uṭajāt tu tatas tasmān niścakrāma sa vai dvijaḥ vapuṣā khaṃ ca bhūmiṃ ca vyāpya vāyur ivodyataḥ
english: Then from that leaf-hut the brahmin came forth, filling sky and earth with his form, like the wind upraised.

sanskrit: svareṇa vipraḥ śaikṣeṇa trīṃl lokān anunādayan uvāca cainaṃ dharmajñaṃ pūrvam āmantrya nāmataḥ
english: With a voice schooled in the sacred chants, the brahmin made the three worlds resound, and, addressing that knower of dharma first by name, said to him:

sanskrit: dharmo 'ham asmi bhadraṃ te jijñāsārthaṃ tavānagha prāptaḥ satyaṃ ca te jñātvā prītir me paramā tvayi
english: "I am Dharma—blessing upon you! I have come to test you, O blameless one; and knowing your truth, my delight in you is supreme."

sanskrit: vijitaś ca tvayā mṛtyur yo 'yaṃ tvām anugacchati randhrānveṣī tava sadā tvayā dhṛtyā vaśīkṛtaḥ
english: "And Death, who follows you—ever seeking a weak point in you—has been conquered by you and brought under your sway by your steadfastness."

sanskrit: na cāsti śaktis trailokye kasya cit puruṣottama pativratām imāṃ sādhvīṃ tavodvīkṣitum apy uta
english: "And there is no power in the three worlds in anyone, O best of men, even to look upon this virtuous wife of yours, devoted to her lord."

sanskrit: rakṣitā tvadguṇair eṣā pativrataguṇais tathā adhṛṣyā yad iyaṃ brūyāt tathā tan nānyathā bhavet
english: "Guarded by your virtues and by her own virtues as a faithful wife, she is inviolable; whatever she should declare, that shall come to pass and not otherwise."

sanskrit: eṣā hi tapasā svena saṃyuktā brahmavādinī pāvanārthaṃ ca lokasya saricchreṣṭhā bhaviṣyati
english: "For she, endowed with her own austerity and an expounder of the sacred lore, shall become the noblest of rivers, for the purification of the world."

sanskrit: ardhenaughavatī nāma tvām ardhenānuyāsyati śarīreṇa mahābhāgā yogo hy asyā vaśe sthitaḥ
english: "With one half she shall be the river named Oghavatī, and with the other half, in body, the greatly fortunate one shall follow you; for the power of yoga stands within her command."

sanskrit: anayā saha lokāṃś ca gantāsi tapasārjitān yatra nāvṛttim abhyeti śāśvatāṃs tān sanātanān
english: "And together with her you shall go to the worlds won by austerity, those everlasting and eternal worlds whence one returns no more."
